chain.label: Pilot's workload-management weakness and limited EMB-500 currency
chain.trigger: the pilot had difficulty with planning and workload management and sometimes became "task saturated," freezing up or fixating on a subtask at the expense of other critical subtasks

chain.label: No ice detection or automatic alerting for ice protection activation on the EMB-500
chain.trigger: The EMB-500 is not equipped with an ice detection system.

chain.label: Part 91 single-pilot operation lacking a second crewmember or Part 121/135 oversight to catch an omission
chain.trigger: in a single-pilot operation, the workload is not divided... and no additional crewmember is present to help detect an error of omission

chain.label: Descent and approach flown in visible moisture with TAT below 5 deg C - structural icing conditions
chain.trigger: for at least 15 minutes during the descent and approach to GAI, the pilot was operating in an environment conducive to structural icing without either airplane ice protection system activated

chain.label: Landing speeds set from the non-icing chart and an understated weight (Vref 92 kt instead of 126 kt)
chain.trigger: the pilot set the landing reference (Vref) speed at 92 knots, indicating that he used performance data for operation with the wing and horizontal stabilizer deice system turned off and an airplane landing weight less than the airplane's actual weight

caused_by.evidence: the accident pilot needed a considerable amount of extra training time to prepare for his EMB-500 check ride... revealed significant weaknesses in his capabilities
Based on the AWOS-reported weather conditions, the pilot should have performed the Descent checklist items that appeared in the Normal Icing Conditions checklist

chain.label: Wing and horizontal stabilizer deice system never reactivated for the descent and approach
chain.trigger: The CVDR recorded no activity or faults during the rest of the flight for either ice protection system, indicating that the pilot did not turn the systems back on.

caused_by.evidence: it is possible that the pilot forgot to activate the wing and horizontal stabilizer deice system during the approach (a relatively high workload phase of flight)
pilots of these airplanes would benefit from a system that provides automatic alerting when the ice protection systems should be activated
14 CFR Part 91 operations do not necessarily share the same regulatory and organizational controls as 14 CFR Part 121 and Part 135 operations
consistent with his referencing the Normal (non-icing) checklist, which does not call for the activation of the wing and horizontal stabilizer deice system

chain.label: Ice accumulated on the unprotected wing and horizontal stabilizer leading edges
chain.trigger: the pilot's failure to use the wing and horizontal stabilizer deice system during the approach... led to ice accumulation

caused_by.evidence: About one-third of these PIREPs indicated structural icing conditions between 2,500 and 5,300 ft
the pilot's failure to use the wing and horizontal stabilizer deice system during the approach to GAI led to ice accumulation

chain.label: Decaying airspeed and rising AOA not recognized; low-speed awareness bands understated the stall speed
chain.trigger: Because the deice system was not activated by the pilot before landing, the band indications (low speed awareness) on the airspeed display did not appropriately indicate the stall warning speed.

caused_by.evidence: if the deice system had been activated, the airspeed tape would have displayed the top of the red band at 102 knots... instead of 87 knots
the airplane's airspeed decreased below 115 knots. The airspeed continued to decrease as the autopilot slowly pitched the airplane up to maintain the RNAV glidepath.

chain.label: Stall developed about 300 ft above field elevation, below the 300-500 ft needed for recovery
chain.trigger: the airplane was at an altitude of about 840 ft (300 ft above field elevation) and about 1 mile from the runway

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall at 88 kt, occurring before the aural stall warning or stick pusher
chain.trigger: an aerodynamic stall occurred shortly before the aural stall warning at 1041:35.9, providing the pilot with no warning of the impending stall

caused_by.evidence: led to ice accumulation, an aerodynamic stall at a higher airspeed than would occur without ice accumulation, and the occurrence of the stall before the aural stall warning sounded or the stick pusher activated
without using the appropriate landing performance speeds for the weather conditions and airplane weight... which together resulted in an aerodynamic stall
the recorded data showed that roll oscillations began and an aerodynamic stall occurred shortly before the aural stall warning

chain.label: Uncontrolled roll oscillations to more than 100 deg right, airplane inverted
chain.trigger: the airplane went through a series of left/right roll oscillations, eventually rolling more than 100º to the right before impact in a left-wing-down attitude

caused_by.evidence: the airplane rolled about 59º to the left and then went through several roll oscillations before returning to wings level and then starting another roll to the right
Once the airplane stalled, its altitude was too low to recover.

chain.label: Impact with three houses and terrain about 3/4 mile short of runway 14, postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted three houses and terrain in a left-wing-down attitude of 110.5º about 4,000 ft from the approach end of runway 14.

caused_by.evidence: he reported seeing the airplane banking to the left, right, and left again, at which time it became inverted and impacted the ground

chain.label: Six fatalities: pilot, two passengers, and three house occupants
chain.trigger: The pilot, the two passengers, and the three people in the house died as a result of the accident.

caused_by.evidence: After the airplane's wing struck the house, the damage and ensuing fire trapped the occupants on the upper floor.
